utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Ms. Loukas, the Chamber is aware of the fact that, although we have not seen it yet, that a motion has been filed yesterday in the afternoon in respect of Witness 382.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And of course the Defence is invited to formulate as soon as possible a response, even if that would be an oral response, which would be totally acceptable under the present circumstances. I just wanted to draw your attention to it so that a surprise comes not any later than necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In fact, I received an e-mail of the filing from Mr. Gaynor from the Prosecution when I got out of court yesterday and in view of the fact that I think that that Witness 382 is -- we could expect him, I imagine, to testify probably tomorrow, I think that an oral response is all that we can offer at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I just wanted to avoid that the surprise would even be greater than it is already.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you for that. I should indicate before we proceed that we were ably assisted with the assistance of an interpreter at our conference with Mr. Krajisnik yesterday, thanks to the efforts of both Ms. Meleras and Ms. Petra Jacoby from the Registry, which was very useful, and their assistance is greatly appreciated. And additionally, I've asked for the assistance of an interpreter during the day today so that we can communicate with Mr. Krajisnik during the breaks and what have you. I can indicate that interpreter is not here yet but I think there is some problem always emerges because Defence counsel are not allowed to bring people into the building and they have to have wait for somebody to bring him in. But at some point --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll greet him whenever he arrives.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you please escort Mr. Alajbegovic into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, while we are waiting, I just wanted to inform the Court that a number of corrections were made yesterday to the OTP statement provided by Mr. Alajbegovic. I am informed that those changes result in a change in construction in the language and therefore -- in the B/C/S version of the statement, therefore the changes aren't so easily entered. I will submit the English changed statement from the OTP to CLSS and get a corrected version from them, and as soon as I get it I will provide it to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. My concern yesterday was that now and then I get the impression that a lot of copying is done even when it's not absolutely necessary, involving huge amounts of paper and -- but of course it should never go to the detriment of the quality of our work. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Alajbegovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I take it that you can hear me in a language you understand. I also take that from your "good morning" response to what I said.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Alajbegovic, please be seated. I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony yesterday and you will now be cross-examined by Ms. Loukas, counsel for the Defence. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and before I proceed, I should mention, as I neglected to mention in fact yesterday that I am ably assisted today by Ms. Kelly Pitcher for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Welcome in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Alajbegovic.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, I want to ask you about your awareness of various matters in relation to your local municipality at the outset. Were you aware in and around March 1992 of Muslims in the Rogatica municipality arming themselves through religious institutions? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And Mr. Alajbegovic, you, yourself, through the police, I suggest to you, were, in fact, involved in the process of arming local Muslims in the Rogatica municipality.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, in relation to the split in the municipality that was negotiated between the SDA and the SDS, you're aware, of course, of a decision to divide the municipality into a Serb part and a Muslim part, and that was a declaration that was signed by the president of the local assembly, Adil Lutvic. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of the declaration, and the Serb side did ask for a division into the Serb side or part and the Muslim part during the negotiations. I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: All right. But you're not aware of the declaration signed by Adil Lutvic; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Were you aware in early April in 1992, when the war had begun elsewhere in Bosnia, of Serbs moving out of Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not going on.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Were you aware of people in your local community, Bosniak Muslims, saying things like "Serbs to Serbia, this is Muslim land"? Were you aware of anything of that nature?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, tell me, on the 6th of May, 1992, were you aware of an attack by Muslim paramilitaries in the -- on the Serb population in the village of Borika?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that never happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Were you aware that during that attack, that Branko Balcak, a Serb man, was killed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I do know about his killing.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Were you aware that his mother was also wounded?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We received information that he had been wounded by a grenade coming from one of the members of the paramilitaries, Serb paramilitaries that were located at Borika.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So you weren't aware that the attack involved Muslim paramilitaries; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that and they couldn't have been involved either.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Of course you weren't present; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point, no, but we received information according to which they said that the Muslim village of Zivaljevic was under -- in danger, under threat, and that was the only village close to where this man Mr. Balcak lost his life.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: So we are in agreement there that you say you weren't aware that Muslim paramilitaries were involved in the killing of Branko Balcak and the severe wounding of his mother; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that means they weren't involved in that, and I'm quite certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, were you aware on the 20th of May, 1992, that Drazenko Mihajlovic from Seljane was killed in the suburban settlement of Zlatni Do?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And again, that was by Muslim paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know about that because I was on the territory of the local commune of Kozlici.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And were you aware that on the same day, the 20th of May, 1992, Milos Vukovic was killed by Muslims in the village of Zivaljevina, near Kovanja?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Were you aware of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, just from my understanding, Zivaljevina, is that different from the village the witness just mentioned, Zivaljevici? Is that --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can indicate that in terms of my questions, the first village I mentioned in relation to the killing of Drazenko Mihajlovic, that was Seljane, which is spelled S-e-l-j-a-n-e.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's just north-east of Rogatica town, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. And perhaps for the benefit of the transcript I might also spell the second area I spoke of, which is Zlatni Do, Z-l-a-t-n-i D-o.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you indicate where that is located, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Not at this point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. And then?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And in relation to the question I gave in relation to Milos Vukovic, the killing of Milos Vukovic by Muslims, that was the village of Zivaljevini, which is spelled Z-i-v-a-l-j-e-v-i-n-i, by Kovanja, which is K-o-v-a-n-j-a.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I still have to locate that, but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour. I will just get my legal assistant to check on those positions to assist the Court while I proceed with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I found it, as a matter of fact. The villages are quite similar in name, Zivaljevin or Zivaljevici, and Kovanja is just north-west of Rogatica. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, were you aware of Muslims leaving these areas around the time of the 20th of May that I have just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And leaving in the sense of voluntarily, of course.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, towards the end of May 1992, were you aware of Bosniak Muslims leaving Rogatica in buses belonging to Tenotrans, which was, of course, shared by a Bosniak Muslim Midhat Pasic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That happened before the 20th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, would you care to put a date on it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the period between the 5th to the 15th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alajbegovic. Now, were you aware of four Bosniak Muslims, in fact a pair of two brothers, who were soldiers in the VRS from the municipality of Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Were you aware of four Bosniak Muslims who were soldiers in the Serbian army, in the --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about two. I know about two men.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes. And I'm speaking, of course, of the Bosnian Serb army.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And who were they?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were two brothers, Izet and Himzo Golic.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And was one of them later on the director of Centrotrans, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He worked in Centrotrans before the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And were you aware of Croats who joined the Bosnian Serb army?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And are you aware that these Bosnian Muslims who joined the army, the Bosnian Serb army, are still in their homes in Rogatica, in the Rogatica municipality?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not live in the urban area of Rogatica but in the village of Zakomo, which is to the north, towards Sokolac. And they didn't declare themselves as Muslims, they declared themselves as Yugoslavs.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, you've given one statement to the Bosnian authorities in 1999 and a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in 1999; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And of course you indicated in your evidence yesterday when you were questioned by Mr. Harmon that you stand by your statements as true and correct, subject to the corrections you made in court yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, just for my information, I read in the transcript, and that's what I heard as well, a statement to the Bosnian authorities in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, it was the ICTY statement that was 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The other one was 1996 but I can imagine that you are a bit confused by the additional date on the top -- on the bottom of each page of the 1996 --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's right, 1999 appears --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It has been cleared, we are talking about the same document.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: But it's interesting that both 1999 and 1996 appear on the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that he identified these documents as the statements he gave in 1996, and he did that in 1999. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Now, you indicated in your evidence yesterday when you were

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: correct, subject to the corrections you made in court yesterday. Rather than nodding, Mr. Alajbegovic, you'll have to give a verbal answer so it can be recorded on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And of course you're a police officer of many years standing, Mr. Alajbegovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And you have experience in assisting in the taking of statements from witnesses throughout your career?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And you are very well aware of what's required in a witness statement; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, prior to signing your statements, in particular the statement to the ICTY, you, of course, were asked prior to signing it if you had anything to add; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And you also knew that when you were giving your statement in 1999 to the Office of the Prosecutor, that they wanted to have from you everything that you knew on the period we're talking about; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. That assumes a fact not in evidence. That assumes that this witness was informed that this person who was taking this statement wanted to know everything that had to do with the period that we're involved in in this indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Isn't it true, Mr. Harmon, that the right of the Defence to put leading questions also includes that where the Prosecution is not entitled to put any question to a witness which suggests a fact not yet established, that the Defence, on the other hand, is entitled to do so because that's one of the -- one of the varieties of what a leading question is. So apart from suggesting the answer, another variety of a leading question is a question which suggests the existence of a fact not yet in evidence. So therefore, if I bring it back to the basics, you are blaming Ms. Loukas for putting the leading question to the witness which she is entitled to do, so the objection is denied. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, you knew, did you not, that when you were giving your statement as a police officer of many years' standing, that when you were giving your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, that they wanted to have from you everything that you knew from the period in question; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But at that moment, I did not talk about everything I knew.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, whenever you might think that you could convince a jury that if we are talking about events of a couple of months that a witness would at all be in a position to tell everything he knows, certainly a professional Bench will not be convinced by that. Come up with whatever relevant, important information he has not mentioned and we'll certainly pay proper attention to that, but these type of questions that just put it to the witness, isn't it true that you would tell everything, and then later on establish that he did not tell everything, of course, it comes down to relevant information not mentioned by the witness. And if I would ask you to tell everything you knew about the last three months, you'd certainly fail. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't know about that. I write a daily diary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, even then, Ms. Loukas. And I would fail as well, and I expect everyone in this courtroom to fail. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will make one point in relation to that, Your Honour, and it's just this: I take on board what Your Honour has indicated, but I would also indicate that a man who has been a police officer for so many years is in a different position to a lay witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course. And even without -- I mean, in assessing and evaluating the evidence of a witness, of course this Court, even -- I do not mind if you draw the attention to that, but just verify that we are aware - and it's just a verification, it's not -- of course this Court will look at a statement of a police officer in a different way as it does look at a statement of a plumber or whatever. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, now, of course, when you provided the statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, you, yourself, as a police officer, wished to provide everything that you considered significant about the period in question; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My statement mostly had to do with the case of Mico Andric, who was indicted at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand that was the context in which your statement to the Bosnian authorities was taken, that was in relation to Mico Andric, but of course your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor in 1999 was, of course, taken in a broader context; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see the witness nodding yes but we'd like to have your answers because it does not appear on paper if you are just nodding.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The statement did not include a broader context.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You're referring -- when you say the statement did not include a broader context, you're talking about your statement to the Bosnian authorities; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the statement given to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me ask you, was your statement to the Tribunal similarly focused on Mr. Andric as the statement you gave to the Bosnian authorities?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No; to a lesser degree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and more -- in general terms, the events that took place at that time. That's what Ms. Loukas referred to as a broader context.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And of course you, yourself, were anxious to ensure that you provided the Office of the Prosecutor, as a police officer of many years' standing, with whatever you knew in relation to potential links with higher authorities; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirmed that yesterday while giving evidence. I thought that I would be giving additional information here and now too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm talking about at the time you gave a statement. Obviously, you are a police officer of many years' standing, a commander, you know how to give a statement, don't you, Mr. Alajbegovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And you know what's required of you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am here and available to tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And obviously the truth is, as a police officer of many years' standing, when you gave your statement to the ICTY Office of the Prosecutor, you knew that you had to provide them with significant information, if you had it, about potential linkages with higher authorities. That is correct, is it not?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement I gave to the Tribunal in Sarajevo shows in all its paragraphs that --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will stop you there, Mr. Alajbegovic. You know very well my question is about your statement to the ICTY. Now, please answer my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, he was answering the question and he was interrupted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because the question was about the ICTY statement and the answer was about the Bosnian statement, so therefore, --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note that the witness said "Tribunal" and in B/C/S when people say Tribunal, it means the ICTY. They never refer to the abbreviation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did the witness -- perhaps I don't know whom to ask, but he was referring to the Tribunal in -- yes. Now I do understand. Ms. Loukas, there is a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Obviously there is an interpretation question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "The statement I gave to the Tribunal..." but not the Tribunal in Sarajevo, but the statement he gave in Sarajevo to the Tribunal, that is the ICTY, so therefore, where I said that you correctly interrupted the witness, upon rereading it, I was similarly confused as you seemed to have been.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. It seems there's been some sort of -- something's been lost in translation, as it were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I think nothing is lost but it's just the way terms are used. So therefore, Mr. Alajbegovic, I think we misunderstood you. When you said, "The statement I gave to the Tribunal in Sarajevo," we Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. understood that you gave a statement to a Tribunal in Sarajevo instead of giving a statement in Sarajevo to the Tribunal, meaning the ICTY.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what Ms. Loukas would like to know is the following: Did you give all information you knew about communication with higher levels of authority when you gave your statement to the investigators of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any important portions you left out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. All those official talks. That would require an additional statement, wouldn't they, with an elaboration of certain requirements made by the negotiators of the Serbian side and the policy that was pursued in the municipality of Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Loukas, then I think that you would be interested to know why.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So Mr. Alajbegovic, you obviously told the people that interviewed you that you had more information?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the statement given at the Tribunal here or the statement I made in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well let's get something straight here, Mr. Alajbegovic. The statement you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor for the ICTY, where was that statement given?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. So both statements were given in Sarajevo, correct; the Bosnian statement and the statement for the Office of the Prosecutor of the -- this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. I am now asking you about the statement you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal in 1999. Do you understand me thus far?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you've told the Court that you did not give all the information in your statement to the Prosecution, and what you left out - this is at the bottom of page 15, the beginning of page 16 - is that -- what you left out was all those official talks. "That would require an additional statement, wouldn't they, with an elaboration made by certain requirements from negotiators of the Serbian side and the policy that was pursued in the municipality of Rogatica." Now, my question, Mr. Alajbegovic, is obviously when you were giving your statement to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor for this Tribunal, you obviously told the people that were interviewing you that you had more information; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is an elaboration of certain theses from the statement given in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you tell the investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor in relation to this Tribunal in 1999 that you had more information?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say that but I thought that I would have an opportunity once again to give additional details and thus expand my original statement. That is the entire state of negotiations that was not described in detail in the statement and now in the context of what I said yesterday when I was giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So Mr. Alajbegovic, how many years have you been a police officer?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my police career started in 1975 and it's still there. That is to say, for all of 30 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Would you care to tell this Tribunal why you left out significant information from your statement as a police officer of 30 years' standing?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything I lived through during the negotiations, and then during the war operations, and during my stay in Gorazde and when I went to Sarajevo, all of that affected me, and it has left certain consequences that I still suffer at this very moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You're not saying that you're incapable of performing your duties as a police officer, are you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you've said. No. I am capable of performing the duties that I do perform.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Alajbegovic. Let's move on to the next topic. Now, in relation to your 1999 statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal, from paragraphs 5 to 10 on the first page -- and it may be useful, I think, if the witness actually has the statement in front of him for these purposes. Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, you deal there on page 2 in the English version, which is paragraphs 6 to 10, on basically the rise of Serb nationalism and some rallies; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And you also gave evidence of this at pages 30 and 32 of -- 30 to 32 of the transcript from yesterday, for the benefit of the -- of Your Honours and the Prosecution. Now, just to place these matters in context, this question of nationalism, Mr. Alajbegovic, you are, of course, aware that when the -- prior to the introduction of the elections, that three major nationalist parties were formed in Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And in fact you'd be aware that the Bosniak Muslim party, the SDA, was, of course, formed prior to the Serbian Democratic Party; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And in terms of the rise of nationalism amongst the various communities in Bosnia, you are, of course, aware that on a visit to Turkey in July 1991, that Mr. Izetbegovic asked to join the Organisation of Islamic Countries. You're aware of that, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Well let me put it to you this way, Mr. Alajbegovic: You've referred in your statement to the rise of Serb nationalism, but you would concede, would you not, that there was a rise in nationalism amongst all three communities in Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Moving on to the next topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, I'd like to ask one additional question in this respect. Mr. Alajbegovic, isn't it true that the three nationalistic parties that were formed -- well, were mainly based on the nationality or ethnicity of the members and that there was a general movement to have the political spectre mainly formed by parties which were not primarily based on political programmes such as you find in other countries - socialist, liberals, et cetera - but that they were mainly driven by the nationality or the ethnicity of those belonging to those parties.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but the Party of Democratic Action had the possibility to have members of other ethnic groups join their ranks, and there were indeed such cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was the SDS -- could you not become a member of the SDS if you were -- if you had reported yourself as Yugoslav or if you were a Muslim or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some people did that too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So to that extent, what I am trying to find out from your evidence is whether all the three groups, that is let me say Croats, Muslims, and Serbs, organised themselves in the political sense in that period of time in accordance with this background rather than with political programmes which were unrelated to the national or ethnic background of the party members.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it depended. Not all three options were based on that principle of homogeneity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You said you could become a member of the SDA even if you were not a Muslim, and at the same time, you say you could become a member of the SDS even if you were not a Serb.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Alajbegovic, are you sure you're not being a Bosniak Muslim advocate rather than an objective witness to this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that I am an objective witness and my objective is to tell the truth, to say what I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, just on this topic of nationalism, were you aware of an SDA rally in Velika Kladusa in September of 1990 in which about 200.000 people attended?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through the media only.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Weren't you aware that there were many green flags and people and -- some people in Arabic dress there? You were aware of that, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that dress. I don't know about it even now. I didn't know about it at that moment either.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Were you aware that there were people there with portraits of Saddam Hussein?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, you were aware, of course, that Mr. Izetbegovic, the SDA leader, was a guest of honour at the SDS inaugural event. You were aware of that, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, moving on to a -- another topic. If we go to page 3 of the English statement, and paragraph 12 in your statement, you talk there about various people going around Serb villages, telling them that there was a Muslim threat, and you've referred to that being -- yes, you've -- in that statement, you've referred to the people from Serb villages -- going to Serb villages and telling that there was a Muslim threat. Now, you were aware of comments, were you not, Mr. Alajbegovic, by --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: If I might have a moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: -- comments by Mr. Zulfikarpasic criticising Mr. Izetbegovic when he said that: "If Slovenia and Croatia were to leave Yugoslavia, we would declare independence for Bosnia and the Muslims would defend it with arms." You were aware of that, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You would concede, wouldn't you, that in that sense the threat that some Serbs might have perceived was not exactly illusory, was it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question is the following: Whether, on the basis of what Ms. Loukas just put to you, that Muslim leaders expressed themselves in terms of independence and to defend that, that it was not just an illusion that some Serbs thought or that Serbs thought that they were in -- that they were under threat and that they were in danger.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes to what? It was not illusory or was it illusory?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was not -- or rather, it was an illusion for the Serb people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the question then is if I say: "I'll defend myself with arms," could that be perceived by others as a threat or as at least a danger?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is a lesser form of danger, but the Serbs knew that the Muslims were not armed and that they did not have a single military unit that would defend them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You were aware, were you not, Mr. Alajbegovic, that there were -- let me put it to you this way --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: And I'm referring here, Your Honours, to evidence given by Witness 659, pages 63 and 64, of the 14th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you just allow me to get the 14th of March on my screen, Ms. Loukas. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You were aware, were you not, that the SDA was arming itself, were you not?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And of course you denied that you were supplying arms to your local community.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now let's --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Or rather, "I'm not." Interpreter's correction, I beg your pardon. "No" meaning he did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you for that correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, let's have another look at your statement, and now we're going to go to paragraphs 3 and 4 -- sorry, that's paragraphs 14 and 15 on page 3 in the English version. And this is a matter that was dealt with in the transcript at pages 42 to 46 yesterday. Now, you've indicated there that you were -- sorry, Your Honour, I've just lost a document. Yes, paragraphs 14 and 15, you have that before you. That you were an eyewitness to the unloading of automatic rifles, machine-guns, hand grenades, RPG, seven rocket-launchers, and ammunition; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And this was a topic on which you were asked some questions by His Honour Judge Hanoteau, and this was an area in which you took no action; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We didn't take any action.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if we look, for example, at -- and I'm now going to page 4 of your statement, which is paragraph 19, you say there that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, before you proceed, could you please clarify, the answer is not entirely clear to me. You put it to the witness that he took no action.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You asked, "Correct?" The answer was, "No. We didn't take any action," which is a bit contradictory. And apart from that, it's not easy to reconcile with the extensive answers he gave to the questions of Judge Hanoteau yesterday where a distinction was made between reporting and taking any action apart from reporting. So it's not clear. It certainly does not assist me at this moment. So if you find it an important matter, I'd like you to further clarify the matter. If you say that's sufficient, then we leave it as it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: It is an area that I may come back to, Your Honour, depending on how much time I ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I didn't want to conceal from you that as it stands now, this part is less assisting than the extensive answers given yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. Yes, I think at this point, Your Honour, in view of the other matters I have to cover and in view of my limited time, I'll proceed to another matter, and if I have some time, I'll come back to this as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, we go to paragraph 19 of your statement. So you there indicate that somebody else witnessed something but the -- basically the only other person that can verify what you're saying there is dead; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information came in through the police station from Stjenice to the effect that Mr. Karadzic, with his escorts, was moving in the direction of Rogatica. The patrol from Rogatica went to the road and then the escorts went to the regional road running from Rogatica to Borika where Mr. Karadzic arrived. He arrived at the facility that is mentioned in paragraph 19, so I received confirmation from up there from a man who was a member of the reserve formation. I gave him your name yesterday and I will be happy to repeat it today if you need it, but unfortunately, in 1997 and 1998, he died a natural death in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, so -- so far we've got you taking no action in relation to what you say occurred at paragraphs 15 and 16; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Practically, we did not take any action, but as far as information goes, I informed my superior, who was the chief of the police station, and as the party president, he probably assessed that it didn't warrant any action in the sense of taking practical steps such as confiscating the weapons from -- and taking it away from the area or preventing it from reaching the area it was intended to reach.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And who was your superior?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of the public security station was Mr. Ismet Osmanovic, and he also acted as president of the democratic -- Party of Democratic Action for the Rogatica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, moving on to another area, and now we're on page 5, which is paragraphs 37 and 38, where you indicate that you saw Mr. Vasiljevic arming the population. And you gave evidence about these matters at pages 39 to 41 of the transcript yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that incorrectly states the evidence. This incident -- the witness testified he received the information about Vasiljevic arming the people. Counsel has stated that, "You indicate that you saw Vasiljevic arming the people." So I think the question contains information that is inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, I was proceeding from the statement that didn't have the correction on it, received information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It has been corrected, especially in this aspect.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So -- and that's an aspect that you corrected that you received information about it, but in any event, that's not the area I want to ask you about. I want to ask you about these photographs. Who took the photographs?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crime inspector of the public security station in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And in relation to these photographs, you've indicated that a photographic album was compiled, correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Page 40 of the evidence from yesterday, Your Honours, at line 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And of course as a good police officer who knows how to protect evidence, you kept a copy yourself as well, didn't you, as the commander?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, a copy remained in the crime police department and another copy I personally took to the department of the crime police of the republican SUP, which was headed by, as assistant minister, Momcilo Mandic. I handed it over to his head of department for that area. I mentioned the man's name yesterday while giving testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now he was a Muslim, of course; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by his name, yes, but I don't know how he declared himself because I noted that he didn't have a Bosnian accent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. In any event, so two copies of these photographs are produced, according to your evidence; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, have the Office of the Prosecutor been able to locate any copies of these photographs?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. I don't actually know.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I might just ask on the record of the Prosecution, Mr. Harmon, if copies of these photographs have been located.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: No, we don't have possession of those photographs, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, pages -- at pages 59 and 60 of the transcript from yesterday, you were again asked some questions by His Honour Judge Hanoteau about reporting various matters. You will recall being asked those questions; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, he was asking you about -- I'll come to a specific question. He asked you, "These are documents you drafted yourself." This is at page 60, line 14 and 15. And your response was, "As I received information and as I went out into the field where I saw many things with my own eyes, I would return to the police station, draft my text, and then send it by teleprinter or teletype to the central base of the SUP, the Secretariat of the Interior." Do you recall giving that answer?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the republican Secretariat for Internal Affairs of Bosnia-Herzegovina during that interval, that's what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, to your knowledge, has the Office of the Prosecutor been able to locate any of these documents that you drafted?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I ask Mr. Harmon to confirm for the court record if any of these documents have been located.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: To my knowledge, they have not, Your Honour. We do not have possession of them. For counsel's benefit, had we had possession of these documents and the photographs, they would have been led into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I can imagine that was the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So therefore, Ms. Loukas, you are spending quite a lot of time on drawing our attention to the fact that although the witness is talking about photographs and reports, that they have not been produced and therefore there's no way to verify the correctness of his answers in this respect. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It took me about 17 seconds, approximately, to draw my own attention to it. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now let's move on to page 86 of the transcript of the evidence that you gave yesterday, and I think that that was at -- let's see, we're dealing with -- yes, pages 85, 86, in relation to a letter, and that's mentioned at paragraph 47 of the statement. You see what I'm talking about there, Mr. Alajbegovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Two copies of that letter?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And you tell the Court that you, as a police officer, tore up the letter; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And of course, to your knowledge, the other copy of the letter can't be found; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it can be found.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, I ask the Prosecution if a copy of this letter has been found.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: The same answer that I gave previously, Your Honour: Had I had a copy of this letter, I would have produced it. I am attempting to try to find that letter. I've made efforts to find that letter, and if I do, I will submit it to the Court and to counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the same time, the witness says that it can be found. Could he tell us how it could be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I can -- the witness provided me --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think it would be better to have the evidence firsthand from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you tell us how it could be found, this letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The letter, one copy of the letter was handed over to the military authorities and it has been stored in the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. files of the 1st Rogatica Brigade, which is located in Gorazde at present, and the intelligence organ has access to it, of the units of the federation in Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the record, that's the same information that I was provided by this witness and I have made efforts to, based on that information, locate this letter, and again I will state if that letter is located, I will present a copy of the letter to the Court and to the Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were these recent efforts?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. I received this information from the witness when he came here and I took that information and immediately made a request for assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I ask you one additional question,

utterances.speaker: MR. ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, in paragraph 47, you give a literal quote, that's what you did in 1999. What made it possible for you to make a literal quote from that letter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The letter made a great impression on me and all those who were informed of the contents of the letter at that time because we realised that the Serb forces and the Serb army were preparing an offensive to cleanse the terrain and to expel us from the hearths that we had been living and occupying for centuries, so we can't forget the text of the letter and I am ready and able at all times to quote it, 90 per cent of what was written in the letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but I may take it that you could not for the full 100 per cent guarantee every word to be literally the words written in that letter because it would require you to keep in your mind for seven years a seven- or eight-line text. I would be hesitant to rely upon my memory under those circumstances. Not about the general content of the letter, but on literally quoting.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You would have the same hesitation; is that a correct understanding of your answer? You do not give a full 100 per cent guarantee that the quote is in every respect a correct quote; is that a correct understanding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but 90 per cent correct, I would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Alajbegovic, you've mentioned a couple of names I just want to take you to. Petar Jesic. Do you remember mentioning that name?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And you're aware that he was not a member of the SDS; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And a Mr. Sokolovic, you were aware that he wasn't a member of the SDS, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: He was a member of Mr. Mirko Pejanovic's party, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, are you prepared to concede the possibility that Mr. Karadzic did not meet with General Milosevic in Borika?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The village is Borika, a weekend house of the former Prime Minister of Yugoslavia, Mr. Dzemal Bijedic, where Rajko Kusic had his headquarters, and I'm quite sure that Karadzic did meet Milosevic there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. So you don't allow for the possibility that that's not correct; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, are you prepared to concede the possibility that the Uzice Corps of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, you are constantly creating confusion. You say, "You do not allow for the possibility; is that correct?" If the witness then says No, that means that it's not correct or that he doesn't allow, but your questions are a source of confusion. Do you understand what I mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I'm happy to ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I take it that --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: But I wouldn't have thought my questions were a source of confusion, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, in this respect, they are. Yes, you say, "Do you allow for the --" "You don't allow for the possibility that that's not correct." That means you are certain --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Perhaps I have fallen into something of a double negative there, Your Honour. I will concede that. I will concede that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Sometimes one gets carried away with the flow of the moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So you don't concede that possibility, correct, Mr. Alajbegovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, moving on to the Uzice Corps of the JNA. You've given evidence in --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Again, Ms. Loukas, if you ask "You don't concede that possibility; correct?" and if the answer is No, then that means that the witness says he concedes that possibility because you ask whether it's correct that he doesn't concede. If he then says No, that means it's not correct that he doesn't concede, so therefore he concedes, and that creates the confusion. Do you understand what I mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, I understand what you mean but I don't think that anyone in the courtroom is unclear about what the witness is saying, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and if you carefully listen to what he says and if you carefully read what he says, the understanding of everyone is exactly opposite from what he actually says, and that's, of course, is situation which is confusing and which should be avoided to the extent possible. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Alajbegovic, you say there's no possibility --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No, I can't do this without going into a double negative. I think I'll leave it alone, quite frankly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You also could ask whether he's perfectly certain that it happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, but it's really quite pointless.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's exactly the same question, and the other question, the way you put them - and you did that not once but you did that several times - is, per se, confusing. Let's not debate it, but perhaps we'll find the moment somewhere in the next six months, a moment to talk about logics and the logic in questioning. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, but -- I'm sorry, Your Honour, but I think we've spent rather a long time on a matter that didn't need so long, quite frankly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's 10.30, anyhow, Ms. Loukas.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether you want to -- whether you would enter a new subject.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I certainly will be, Your Honour, but I think I will leave possibilities and double negatives alone for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Ms. Loukas, looking at the clock, do you have in mind how much time you'd still need?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't think I have much further to go with this witness, quite frankly, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say, "I need another five minutes," we'd --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I'm certainly not talking about five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, but let's say within half an hour, you would expect to ...

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: I would expect within half an hour, allowing for no possibilities of double negatives, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it saves some time. You would then stay just within the 60 per cent, which is not an absolute rule but -- so please be confident that there's no problem in that respect. We'll adjourn until five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, you may escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, prior to the break, I think we were dealing with this question of General Milosevic, a matter that you covered in paragraph 20 of your ICTY statement of 1999. Now, in that portion of your statement, you deal with this visit of Colonel Dragomir Milosevic and Mr. Radovan Karadzic; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you just tell me which paragraph it is?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It's paragraph 20, Mr. Alajbegovic.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, if I were to tell you that our investigations reveal that Colonel Dragomir Milosevic was not there at that time, would that in any way change your evidence?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in relation to the evidence you've given about the Uzice Corps of the JNA being in the Rogatica municipality on the 19th of May, 1992, if I were to tell you that our investigations thus far reveal that that corps was not there on the 19th of May 1992 or anywhere around that period, would that in any way change your evidence?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, going on to another topic, you gave evidence at pages 71 and 74 of yesterday's transcript in relation to Mr. -- let's see, we're talking about the negotiations here, and you indicated in your evidence that you said, and this is page 71 at line 12: "Mr. Tomo, what does all that mean? What does all this mean?" And you said in evidence that his answer was this: "He said we can't wait any longer because there is enormous pressure being exerted on us by the Main Board of the SDS and the military command and that the SAO of Romanija had already been formed and that this coincided with what I said in my statement and I stated again that Rogatica officially belonged to the SAO Romanija, that they couldn't wait any longer because pressure was being brought to bear against them to get the job done." Do you recall that question and answer, Mr. Alajbegovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And you also gave evidence at page 74, line 10, in response to a question from Judge Orie, you said, "With every conversation, every dialogue that we had, they always said that they would report to the Main Board of the SDS in Pale. Whether they really did so, I don't know, but that's what they said at the negotiations." You recall that further answer in relation to that topic; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, this question of there being conversations with Mr. Batinic and others with an expressed pressure coming from the Main Board of the SDS, that's just simply not the truth, is it, Mr. Alajbegovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the truth that pressure was brought to bear and that that is what they were saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Okay. And of course you were aware in 1999 that this conversation supposedly happened; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yeah, you were aware of it when you gave your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Okay. If the witness might be shown his two statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Can you tell me where, in either of those statements, you mention anything about the Main Board of the SDS, Mr. Alajbegovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Perhaps the Prosecution might care to concede that it does not appear.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On page 3 of my statement, it says, "Parallel with the arming of the Serb population, there were ongoing actions of the SDS party aimed at disarming the Muslim population." This can directly be linked to the context of the orders of the Main Board of the SDS that were being sent to the local SDS board in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Alajbegovic, you did not mention to the investigators this conversation with Mr. Batinic about the Main Board of the SDS or any conversations in relation to pressure coming from the Main Board of the SDS, did you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is mentioned in the context of this conference of Batinic in terms of what it should mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You didn't mention the Main Board of the SDS, did you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was omitted, but the statements made by Batinic at the time as negotiator of the SDS were moving along those lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, the point is clear, unless there's any further detail which we should know about, but your point is perfectly clear to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Let's move on to another topic, a topic in which you gave evidence at page 86, 85 and 86 of the transcript from yesterday. This is in relation to that topic of the letter. Here we have a question from Judge Orie. The question was: "What was more in the letter which is not quoted here? I would like to ask you very much to focus on it because the other information we have read, the statement, so therefore we are aware of that. Please proceed." And your response was: "Right. The letter, the next portion says the Muslim population, so 'population,' the word 'population' there is missing, and the signature is the SDS of Rogatica permissions office. That is what is missing here in this letter." Do you recall that portion of your evidence yesterday?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, just for the sake of the transcript, I'm quoted --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- but the start of the quotation marks should be before "The question was..." It was actually not my question but I put to the witness a question which he did not seem to fully understand at that moment. So therefore the quotation marks should not start with, "What was more in the letter," but should start with, "The question was: What was more in the letter..." Because that's what the transcript says. It says, "The question was: What was more in the letter..." Do you understand what I mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Oh, I see what Your Honour is saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because it was not my question.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour. Well, of course I didn't insert the quotation mark, but just for the record that -- it's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just for the record, that is clear. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honour, and the record is clear. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, of course you recall giving that answer on page 86 of the transcript. You've got the statements in front of you.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: It's not included, this SDS signature, in your statements, is it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not included. It was addressed to the SDS office in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: So that doesn't appear on either of the statements that you gave; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but it's true. I stated it yesterday here, and it has to do with the letter. Everything that I did not say in my statement, I confirmed here yesterday all the things that were missing. That is to say that in the letter it said that buses would be provided for the civilian population in order to relocate them to the central parts of Bosnia where the Muslim population is supposed to live from Visoko to Zenica. That is missing from my statement and I confirmed it yesterday here.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: If the witness might be shown a copy of the supplemental information sheet, dated 25th of March, 2005.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, you had a conference --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we have a B/C/S version of that supplemental information sheet?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can continue asking questions while it is found.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Mr. Alajbegovic, you, of course, had a conference with the Prosecutor on the 25th of March. Last Friday; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And you were asked to provide any corrections you might have of your statements; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They asked me whether I abided by this statement or whether I had any corrections to make in view of the statement, so that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, in your supplemental information sheet, you don't even mention this additional bit of the letter in relation to the SDS Rogatica signature on the document, do you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The office of the SDS in Rogatica, that's what it said and I insisted on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Did you tell the Prosecutor that during your conference on the 25th of March?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I told him and I also said where the letter could be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I accept responsibility for that oversight. Indeed, this witness did tell me that and I did not enter that into the supplemental information sheet. I apologise to counsel and I apologise to the Court for this sheet being incomplete but the witness did inform me of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let's move on to another topic, shall we, Mr. Alajbegovic. And I'm now going to evidence you gave at page 57 of the transcript from yesterday. Beginning on page 56, for the benefit of Your Honours and the Prosecution, you gave this answer in response to a question which was: "Did you have conversations with Rajko Kusic where he made assertions as to the territory of Rogatica?" And Mr. Harmon says to you, "You have to answer the question aloud," and your response was: "Yes, I can answer very specifically. From September 1991 until the beginning of 1992, Rajko Kusic called me up two or three times offering me maps and telling me that this was Serbian territory. He produced coloured maps which I received as preposterous, but on the second and third time he was more insistent and even tried to intimidate me, saying that if we insist on seceding from Yugoslavia, we would be deported and expelled unless we pledged loyalty to Serbs because they considered they Rogatica to be part of Serb territory:" Now, you recall giving that answer, Mr. Alajbegovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And if we also go to page 92 of the transcript, and that's at the bottom of page 92, you said in response to a question from Judge Orie, you gave this response: "Furthermore, the ultimatums expressed in the negotiations to surrender weapons, to be loyal to Serb authorities, failing which we would be deported and ethnically cleansed from those areas proved to be true in other territories. In those three areas along those three axes where Muslim forces were concentrated, operations were later developed such as the Zepa enclave operation and these areas were cleansed from the Muslim population. That is another fact." Do you recall giving that answer?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, you've there indicated that the terms that were used in the ultimatums by the negotiators were "deported or expelled"; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Those specific terms; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And of course when you gave your statements, you were aware that those were the specific words used "deported or expelled"; correct? I'm talking about your statements to the Bosnian authorities and to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, all right. I mean, that's the context of the Bosniak dialect, so it's a bit ambiguous, but deportation, expulsions and ethnic cleansing have the same objective.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: You did not express these ultimatums in your statements as threats of deportation or expelled, did you, Mr. Alajbegovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but all of that had to do with expulsions and ethnic cleansing, an ultimatum, loyalty; if not, then the terrain would be cleansed in order to have the population deported from the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, you, as a police officer of 30 years and a commander, know how important it is to use the specific words in your statement that you say were actually used, don't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, the reason those words do not appear in your statement is because you are not telling the truth in your evidence in chief about those words specifically being used. That's what I'm suggesting to you.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you said, but I was telling the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alajbegovic, I put it to you one last time: I suggest that you are being an advocate for the Muslim cause rather than giving objective evidence before this Trial Chamber as a police officer that will assist the interests of justice. And I take it you would disagree with that proposition; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: That is that you disagree with the proposition I've just put to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree with what you said. I'm not a lawyer for the Muslim people. I am here in the role of witness and I wish to say the truth. The truth is everything that could be established here yesterday through my statements.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Loukas. Mr. Harmon, do you have any need -- is there any need to reexamine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is a need merely to clarify the record that was made yesterday, and I would like to direct the witness's attention and Your Honours' attention to page 42 of the transcript from yesterday. This relates to paragraphs 14 and 15 in the English statement to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yesterday, Mr. Alajbegovic -- first of all, Mr. Alajbegovic, you have the statements in front of you and can you turn to paragraphs 14 and 15 and you will see that paragraphs 14 and 15 of the transcript deal with your being an eyewitness to the unloading of weapons.
